In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a general framework for a finite-strain implementation of a constituting model for cold forming of ceramics.

the following aspects: 1) the development of a finite-strain framework for a constitutive formulation capable of describing powder compaction; 2) the development and testing of an incremental scheme compatible with this finite-strain formulation; and 3) the development and validation of a finite element implementation of the model.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the finite-strain formulation developed here can be used to describe a variety of powder compaction processes.

the proposed formulation and implementation of the constitutive model are able to describe satisfactorily the transition from granulated to dense state, as well as the related mechanical response, in the cold forming of ceramic powders, and the related numerical implementation is able to capture the main features of the mechanical response of the material.

, in the present formulation, the finite-strain constitutive model is solved with a return-mapping algorithm, in which the elastic predictor is a neo-Hooke type of elastic predictor, the plastic corrector is a consistent tangent, and the plastic flow rule is a generalized Drucker–Prager type of flow rule.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the proposed constitutive framework, together with the related finite-strain formulation, can be implemented in a general-purpose FE code, and that this implementation is capable of capturing the transition from granulation to densification during cold forming of ceramics.

the constitutive model for cold compaction of ceramic powder has been implemented in the FE code ABAQUS/Standard, and the numerical results obtained for the compaction of a spherical particle have been compared with the experimental data.

the constitutive model and its finite-strain formulation have been successfully implemented in the finite element code ABAQUS/Standard, and the resulting code has been validated by comparison with experimental data for the compaction of alumina powder.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed formulation can be implemented in a finite element framework, and it is able to capture the transition from granulation to densification in a powder compact.

the proposed formulation is capable of describing the full compaction process from the initial loose powder to the final fully dense material, and that the numerical implementation is stable and efficient, as demonstrated by the results obtained from the FE simulations of a number of simple tests.
the proposed finite-strain formulation, together with the proposed numerical implementation, allows the constitutive model to be used for the simulation of powder compaction at large strains.
